rationale: Many reviews exist, overlap heavily and differ in quality (c3), and the committee needs to know where they agree and where they are silent. An umbrella review with reviews as the unit of analysis, a validated quality rating, an overlap calculation and patient-reported understanding as the primary outcome answers that. The retrieved reviews support professional over ad hoc interpretation (c1), leave video against in-person unsettled for understanding (c2), and show understanding is rarely measured (c4). The 'landmark' equivalence trial suggested by the model is an unverified lead and is not used.
alternatives: New systematic review of primary studies (refused: would duplicate existing reviews within the time available)
Rely on the most recent review only (refused: reviews differ in scope and quality, and overlap must be assessed)
Local comparison of video and in-person understanding (deferred: the right next step if the overview confirms the gap)
whyNotMoreComplex: A new review of primary studies would take far longer and repeat the same small studies; the overview answers the committee's question within the approved analyst time.

decision.statement: Conduct an umbrella review of published reviews on professional, bilingual-staff and ad hoc interpretation, with patient-reported understanding as the primary outcome, review quality rated with AMSTAR 2 and overlap handled with the corrected covered area, and report the video against in-person question as unsettled unless the overview finds higher-confidence evidence.
decision.question: What evidence should inform the network's interpreter standard and its investment in in-person versus video interpreters?

criteria.text: Reviews are numerous, overlapping and of mixed quality, so an overview adds value.
A higher-confidence review already establishes equivalence of video and in-person interpretation for understanding.

gates.requirement: Analyst time for screening, extraction and quality rating
gates.evidence: Language services approval LS-2026-07 for two days a week from October 2026 to March 2027, supplied by the investigator
Library request LIB-LS-2026-33, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: New systematic review of primary studies
Rely on the most recent review only
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c4 from retrieved records; the unverified 'landmark' lead is not cited.

summary: Umbrella review recommended; the video question reported as open; both gates met.
